c.tagline: Sweden's easygoing second city - seafood, canals, cafes, and the west-coast archipelago.

taxi.fareNote: Sweden deregulated taxis, so fares vary sharply by company - check the price-comparison sticker (jamforpris) in the window before riding. Reputable firms include Taxi Goteborg, Taxi Kurir, and TaxiKurir; Uber and Bolt also operate.

emergency.note: 112 is the single European emergency number for police, fire, and ambulance.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_desc: The historic core 'within the moat', laced with canals, the Kungsportsavenyn gateway, shopping streets, and the main train station; central and walkable, the classic first-timer base.
An elegant 19th-century district of stone Renaissance-style buildings just off Kungsportsavenyn ('Avenyn'), packed with restaurants, bars, museums, and the Vasa church; lively dining and nightlife.
Gothenburg's oldest quarter, famous for cobbled Haga Nygata, wooden landshovdingehus, antique shops, and cosy cafes serving giant cinnamon buns; charming and browsable.
The trendy area around leafy Linnegatan and Jarntorget, full of bars, bistros, vintage shops, and Slottsskogen park on its doorstep; a favourite for going out and people-watching.
A bohemian, working-class harbour district west of the centre, known for artists, second-hand shops, food co-ops, and an easygoing creative vibe.

water.note: Tap water is excellent and safe everywhere.

transit.hours: Trams and buses run from about 5:00 AM to midnight, with night services (Flexlinjen / night buses) on weekends.
transit.note: Vasttrafik runs the network: Gothenburg has the largest tram system in Northern Europe (the backbone of city travel), plus buses and the Styrsobolaget archipelago ferries. One ticket covers all modes.
transit.pay: Buy tickets in the Vasttrafik To Go app (cheapest), from ticket machines, or tap a contactless bank card on board; there is no cash on trams or buses.

ferry: Stena Line ferries to Denmark and Germany
train: Gothenburg Central Station (SJ high-speed to Stockholm, regional Vasttag, Oresundstag to Malmo/Copenhagen)

transit.m: Flygbussarna airport coach to the city centre / Nils Ericson Terminal (~30 min, every 15-20 min)
Taxi to the city centre (~30-40 min)

tip.r: Service is included; rounding up or ~5-10% for good service is appreciated but never expected.

food.name: Raksmorgas (shrimp sandwich)
food.desc: A mountain of hand-peeled North Sea shrimp piled on buttered bread with egg, mayonnaise, lettuce, dill and roe; Gothenburg's signature lunch.

places.name: Feskekorka fish hall
places.note: The 1874 fish-church market, reopened after renovation; counters build the sandwich from that morning's catch.

places.name: Heaven 23
places.note: Famous King Size shrimp sandwich on rye with egg and vendace roe, 23 floors up with a city view.

places.name: Sjobaren
places.note: Cosy seafood bar in the old Haga quarter, a local standby for shrimp sandwiches and fish soup.

food.name: West coast oysters and shellfish
food.desc: Bohuslan oysters, langoustines, brown crab and blue mussels straight off the cold Skagerrak coast, usually served raw or simply boiled with aioli.

places.name: Sjomagasinet
places.note: Waterfront seafood institution in an 18th-century warehouse; the benchmark for West Coast shellfish platters.

places.name: Fiskekrogen
places.note: Old-town classic with a big seafood plateau and an oyster bar; long-time city favourite.

places.name: Feskekorka fish hall
places.note: Buy oysters by the piece at the market counters and eat them on the spot.

food.name: Fisksoppa (West Coast fish soup)
food.desc: Creamy saffron-tinged broth loaded with cod, salmon, mussels and shrimp, served with aioli and bread; a Gothenburg lunch staple year round.

places.name: Sjobaren
places.note: Generous, unfussy fish soup in a wooden-beamed Haga dining room; good value at lunch.

places.name: Fiskekrogen
places.note: Refined version with a heavy hand on the shellfish; served with saffron aioli.

places.name: Feskekorka fish hall
places.note: The market restaurants ladle out soup made from whatever came in that morning.

food.name: Janssons frestelse and husmanskost
food.desc: Jansson's temptation is a creamy gratin of potato, onion and sprat fillets; it heads a wider menu of Swedish home cooking like meatballs and pyttipanna.

places.name: Weise
places.note: Old-school Gothenburg beer hall serving proper husmanskost with dark beer and snaps.

places.name: Tullen
places.note: Long-running neighbourhood krog doing classic Swedish home cooking with a daily lunch board.

places.name: Restaurang Familjen
places.note: Modern bistro that reworks husmanskost with seasonal Swedish produce.

food.name: Toast Skagen
food.desc: Fried bread topped with shrimp bound in dill mayonnaise and creme fraiche, finished with a spoon of bleak roe and lemon; the classic Swedish starter.

places.name: Fiskekrogen
places.note: Textbook toast Skagen with a generous load of roe; a reliable old-town order.

places.name: Sjobaren
places.note: Does a homely, shrimp-heavy version as a starter before the fish soup.

places.name: Weise
places.note: Serves it as a bar snack alongside the beer, in a proper wood-panelled room.

food.name: Kanelbulle and fika buns
food.desc: Cardamom-scented cinnamon buns are the heart of fika; Gothenburg's Haga quarter bakes the outsized Hagabulle, roughly the size of a dinner plate.

places.name: Cafe Husaren
places.note: Home of the giant Hagabulle; one bun genuinely feeds a table of two or three.

places.name: Brogyllen
places.note: Patisserie dating to 1874, the traditional address for a well-dressed fika.

places.name: Sol Bageri och Kaffe
places.note: Modern craft bakery turning out warm-from-the-oven cinnamon buns and locally roasted coffee.

food.name: Gothenburg craft beer
food.desc: The city drives Sweden's craft scene, with Stigbergets, Poppels, Dugges and Beerbliotek pouring hoppy pale ales and stouts across the west side.

places.name: Stigbergets Bar
places.note: Taproom of the city's best-known craft brewery, pouring its own fresh hoppy beers.

places.name: Olrepubliken
places.note: Central beer bar with a rotating wall of Swedish and Gothenburg taps.

places.name: Brewers Beer Bar
places.note: Well-curated tap list of local and Nordic breweries in a relaxed street-corner room.

food.name: Aquavit snaps
food.desc: Caraway and dill-spiced grain spirit drunk ice cold in small glasses with pickled herring, shrimp or crayfish; the traditional seafood chaser.

places.name: Sjomagasinet
places.note: Serves a proper snaps selection to go with the shellfish platters.

places.name: Weise
places.note: Beer-hall setting where snaps with herring is the standard order.

places.name: Fiskekrogen
places.note: Keeps a range of Swedish aquavits chilled for the seafood menu.

landmarks: Liseberg
Scandinavia's largest amusement park charms all seasons with wooden coasters, gardens and one of Europe's most magical Christmas markets.
Haga District
Gothenburg's oldest quarter of cobbled lanes and wooden houses is the home of fika, famous for cinnamon buns the size of dinner plates.
Feskekôrka (The Fish Church)
This 1874 fish market's Gothic-arched hall really does resemble a church, a temple to shrimp sandwiches, oysters and West Coast seafood culture.
Gothenburg Archipelago (Southern Islands)
Car-free islands like Styrsö and Vrångö lie a tram-and-ferry ride away, offering smooth granite bathing rocks, fishing hamlets and sea-lavender walks.
Götaplatsen and the Poseidon Statue
Carl Milles' muscular Poseidon presides over the city's cultural acropolis of Art Museum, concert hall and theatre at the Avenue's crest.
Universeum
A seven-storey science centre where visitors wander a humid indoor rainforest, shark tunnel and space exhibits, ideal for rainy Nordic days.
Slottsskogen
The city's beloved central park mixes strolling paths with free-entry Nordic animals, including the penguins, seals and moose every Gothenburger grew up visiting.
Skansen Kronan
A squat 17th-century hilltop redoubt crowned with a golden crown, whose grassy slopes give one of the best free views over Haga's rooftops.
Gothenburg Botanical Garden
One of Europe's finest botanical gardens climbs from formal beds into wild rock gardens and rhododendron valleys covering 175 hectares.
Nya Älvsborg Fortress
A 17th-century island fortress guarding the river mouth, reached by summer boat tours recounting sieges, prisoners and Sweden's naval past.

intl.to: Copenhagen (Denmark) - via Malmo and the Oresund Bridge

train.note: Everything arrives at Gothenburg Central, which shares a concourse with the Nils Ericson coach terminal, so train-to-bus transfers are a two-minute walk. Vy's Oslo trains take a little under four hours and are far cheaper booked ahead; SJ high-speed services reach Stockholm in around three hours, and there are frequent through trains to Copenhagen via Malmo, roughly four hours. Danish and Swedish fares sit on separate systems, so compare sj.se with dsb.dk for the Copenhagen leg. The Oresund crossing is inside Schengen but Denmark runs intermittent ID checks, so carry a passport or national ID card.

bus.note: Long-distance coaches use the Nils Ericson terminal right beside Gothenburg Central, so there is no trek across town. FlixBus (https://www.flixbus.com/) is the main international operator, reaching Oslo in about 3.5-4 hours and Copenhagen in roughly 4.5 hours; tickets are online only and cheapest weeks ahead. Domestic coaches to Stockholm, Malmo and Jonkoping are run by FlixBus and Vy Buss (https://www.vybuss.se/). Danish-bound services are occasionally stopped for ID checks at the bridge.

intl.to: Frederikshavn (Denmark) - sails from the Denmark Terminal at Masthugget, near the centre
Kiel (Germany) - sails from the Germany Terminal at Majnabbe
Southern Gothenburg archipelago - Styrso, Vrango and other islands, from Saltholmen at the end of tram 11

ferry.note: Gothenburg has two Stena Line terminals close to the city: Masthugget for Frederikshavn in Denmark, about 3.5 hours with several sailings a day, and Majnabbe for Kiel in Germany, roughly 14 hours as an overnight crossing with cabins. Cars need booking well ahead in summer and around public holidays; foot passengers rarely do. The old ferry to Newcastle ceased in 2006 and there is no longer any passenger sailing to Britain, only freight. Year-round archipelago ferries to the southern islands leave from Saltholmen on an ordinary Vasttrafik ticket, and no cars are allowed on those islands.

half.name: Marstrand
half.blurb: Fortified island town on the Bohuslän coast, built around the 17th-century Carlsten Fortress and a yacht-filled harbor.

half.name: Fjällbacka
half.blurb: Bohuslän fishing village of granite cliffs and pastel houses, made famous as the setting of Camilla Läckberg's crime novels.

half.name: Varberg
half.blurb: Coastal town with a moated 13th-century fortress that now houses a museum displaying the Bocksten Man bog body.

half.name: Tjörn
half.blurb: Archipelago island connected by bridge, known for its sculpture park, fishing villages, and rugged granite coastline.

half.name: Läckö Slott
half.blurb: Baroque castle on a peninsula in Lake Vänern, with over 200 rooms and formal gardens open to visitors.
